I just sit there feeling completely weighed down by it all. Well, let's see... if I really look back at the calendar, I'd say this... this persistent low has been going on for about a month now. Restless? No, no, it's actually the exact opposite. I definitely don't have trouble sitting still right now. If anything, I have trouble getting moving at all. It's like my whole body and my brain are just moving through molasses.

I'm just... stuck in slow motion. Weight? Well, yes, actually. Now that you mention it, I have. It's not something I've been doing on purpose, you know, I haven't been on a diet or trying to count calories or anything like that. I just sit there feeling completely weighed down by it all. I keep trying to push through it, thinking if I just get to the weekend or just go to sleep a little earlier it will pass, but the heaviness is just always there, making every little daily task feel like a monumental effort...\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?\n\nPatient: Sad... yes, I suppose so. It’s almost more of a... well, most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It’s just right there the second I regain consciousness. It's like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts, if that makes any sense. \n\nI’ll just lie there looking at the ceiling, listening to the alarm go off—I actually changed the tone recently to this soft chime because the old buzzing was just too much to handle with how down I've been feeling—and I just think, 'Oh, here we go again.' But now, I just leave the radio off. I drive in total silence because everything just feels so muted and, well, sad. \n\nThe whole world just feels sort of drained of color, and I can't seem to shake it no matter how much I try to just put on a brave face for my staff. I really try to hide it at the office, because as a manager you have to set the tone, but inside it’s just this pervasive, inescapable grayness that hangs over me all day long.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that you're no longer enjoying activities that you used to find pleasurable?\n\nPatient: Yes, actually... that’s... that’s been really bothering me. I’ve got all my watercolors and acrylics out, and normally, that’s my sanctuary.
